summary: Elevated API key use after clicking stego-image link embedded in onboarding email
description:
Issue summary:
Customer/internal report that several service account API keys showed elevated privilege usage within a 20-minute window after a handful of employees clicked an onboarding email containing an embedded PNG. Impact: potential API key compromise and unauthorized calls to internal admin endpoints.

Impact:
- Multiple service-account API keys issued to new hire onboarding automation made calls to admin/organization/keys and admin/billing endpoints (read-only and write attempts observed).
- No confirmed data exfil, but suspicious token refresh patterns and new ephemeral tokens were minted.
- Affected systems may include console UI, API gateway, and a small set of internal agent services.

Environment:
- prod-us-west primary, spikes also visible in prod-us-east (proxied traffic).
- New-hire onboarding automation service (onboard-agent-v2) and associated CI user tokens appear involved.

Steps to reproduce / How detected:
1) 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC Security automation alerted on anomalous admin API calls from IPs not previously seen for these service accounts.
2) On-call checked correlate logs in api-gateway and noticed a cluster of requests coming immediately after employees opened an onboarding welcome email.
3) Email contained an inline PNG (welcome_badge.png). Recovering the image payload from the mail archive showed an unusual payload size and a base64 blob in metadata.
4) Replaying the sequence in a sandbox (isolated environment) by rendering the PNG triggered an outbound HTTP callback to an external domain and a subsequent redirect to a shortlink.

Initial evidence / logs:
- api-gateway access logs (see excerpts in related_confluence_pages) show admin endpoints hit by tokens tied to service accounts onboard-agent-01..03 between 2026-03-10 09:10-09:30 UTC.
- Token issuance logs show refreshes at unusual intervals and refreshes originating from a user agent string matching the desktop email client.
- Mail logs indicate the outbound email was rendered by Marketing via SendGrid; the embedded PNG metadata contains a 4KB base64 chunk with non-image signature.

Hypothesis:
- The PNG contained a steganographic payload that triggered the email client (or a preview service) to make an HTTP request to an external callback, leaking an authentication artifact (session cookie or token exchange) which allowed the attacker to exchange for ephemeral API keys OR to trigger a server-side callback that used internal credentials during processing.

Immediate mitigation performed:
- Revoked affected service account API keys and rotated credentials for onboard-agent-v2 at 2026-03-10 10:05 UTC.
- Invalidated active SSO sessions for users who opened the email (targeted invalidation) and forced global SSO reauth for the org at 2026-03-10 10:25 UTC.
- Blocked the external domain at perimeter and WAF rules updated to drop requests to the observed callback host.
- Disabled email rendering previews in the internal mail sandbox and removed the specific email from queued sends.

Next actions planned:
- Full token audit across org and reissue of any tokens created in that window.
- Deep analysis of the image metadata and reproduction of the stego payload in a controlled environment.
- Forensics on affected hosts and any services that performed callbacks while processing email assets.
- Engage Legal and CISO for possible disclosure and coordinate with Marketing for a send-source review.
- Update onboarding automation to require stricter validation of external assets and to run asset rendering in an isolated environment with no credential access.
investigation_notes:
Timeline summary and findings to date:
- 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC: Anomaly detection fired on admin endpoint rate and SSO refresh pattern; alert routed to #sec-ops.
- 09:18 UTC: Confirmed cluster of admin calls all signed with tokens issued within previous 30 minutes.
- 09:40 UTC: Mail team provided raw MIME for the onboarding welcome email; discovered embedded PNG has a 4096-byte base64 blob in tEXt chunk.
- 10:00 UTC: Sandbox rendering of PNG caused HTTP POST to hxxp://img-callback[.]host/collect and redirect to a shortlink. Outbound request included an Authorization header when run under the user's environment due to automatic credential forwarding from internal proxy.
- 10:05 UTC: Rotated keys and invalidated sessions.
- Forensic note: No evidence yet of lateral movement beyond admin API calls; storage buckets and customer data show no access outside normal read patterns.
- Risk: medium-high until full token audit completes.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:25 UTC - Arjun Patel (oncall-sre): Initial triage: observed 6 unique service-account tokens calling admin endpoints. Temporarily throttled admin endpoints from suspect IP ranges. Pls attach API gateway excerpts.

2026-03-10 09:38 UTC - Lina Gomez (sec-analyst): Mail team found embedded PNG. Attaching MIME. PNG contains unexpected tEXt chunk with base64. Reproduced callback in isolated container. Looks like stego payload. Recommend immediate key rotation for any tokens active in window.

2026-03-10 10:07 UTC - Arjun Patel (oncall-sre): Keys rotated for onboard-agent-v2 and three service accounts. Forced SSO reauth for impacted users. WAF rules applied to block img-callback.host. Monitoring for retry patterns.

2026-03-10 12:45 UTC - Theo Ramirez (marketing): Confirming this was a one-off send from a small onboarding batch. We're suspending further sends and will provide the source asset and templates for review.

2026-03-11 08:20 UTC - CISO (Priya Nair): Please coordinate with Legal; preserve all raw email artifacts and host network captures. Also prepare a short summary for execs if customer data is affected.

2026-03-12 14:05 UTC - Arjun Patel (oncall-sre): Follow-up: token audit in progress, approx 87 tokens issued in window; 9 were used for admin endpoints and revoked. No further suspicious calls after mitigations. Continuing monitoring.
2026-03-12 16:30 UTC - Maya Chen (reporter): Requesting post-incident runbook update item and checklist for Marketing to prevent future embedded assets from containing active content.
resolution: Mitigations applied: revoked affected API keys, forced targeted SSO reauth, blocked callback domain, suspended offending email batch. Token audit and forensics ongoing. Post-incident action items created: update onboarding asset handling, add stego detection to mail pipeline, and coordination with Marketing and Legal for follow-up.
